terms.definition: A ready-made operation that runs one or more blocks of code when it starts.
terms.example: Wrap the work in a block operation.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let op = BlockOperation { print("hello") }
op.start()
print(op.isFinished)

terms.definition: A queue that runs operation objects and lets you set how many run at once.
terms.example: Add the work to the operation queue.

terms.definition: A rule that makes one operation wait until another operation has finished.
terms.example: An operation dependency keeps the right order.

Learn to explain how to order and limit work with operations: Block Operation, Operation Queue & Operation Dependency, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Block Operation - A ready-made operation that runs one or more blocks of code when it starts.
Operation Queue - A queue that runs operation objects and lets you set how many run at once.
Operation Dependency - A rule that makes one operation wait until another operation has finished.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Block Operation, Operation Queue and Operation Dependency in English?

dialogue.title: Download, then show
dialogue.setting: Work that must run in a fixed order

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I need to download a file and then show it on screen. How do I order the work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an operation queue. An operation queue runs operation objects and can limit how many run at once.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A block operation is the easiest one. It runs a block of code when it starts, like `get` in your code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An operation dependency. It makes one operation wait until another has finished.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You never added the operations to the queue. A block operation does not start by itself there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh no, my mistake. I only set `maxConcurrentOperationCount`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add both to the operation queue, and the operation dependency does the rest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It works! First get, then show.
Wrap the work in a block operation.
